cards.title: Human bodies genuinely glow in the dark
cards.body: The human body emits visible light, glowing with an intensity about one thousand times weaker than our naked eyes can detect. This ultra-weak photon emission is a byproduct of biochemical reactions: metabolic cellular respiration produces free radicals that react with lipids and proteins, emitting tiny pulses of light. Using ultra-sensitive cryogenic cameras, researchers found that our bioluminescent glow ebbs and flows throughout the day, peaking in late afternoon.

sources.title: Imaging of Ultraweak Spontaneous Photon Emission from Human Body Displaying Diurnal Rhythm

cards.title: Deep inside Jupiter, hydrogen is squeezed into a liquid metal
cards.body: Under extreme interior pressure millions of times greater than Earth's atmosphere, hydrogen gas undergoes an exotic phase change. Its molecules break apart and their electrons are squeezed free, flowing as an ocean of liquid metallic hydrogen. This churning, electrically conductive metallic fluid occupies much of Jupiter's vast interior, acting like a colossal dynamo that generates the most powerful planetary magnetic field in our solar system.

cards.title: The beetle that fires boiling chemical explosions from its rear
cards.body: When threatened, the bombardier beetle initiates a violent chemical reaction inside a reinforced abdominal chamber. By mixing stored hydroquinone and hydrogen peroxide with catalytic enzymes, it instantly triggers an explosive exothermic reaction. The mixture flashes to 100 degrees Celsius and violently expels in a rapid, machine-gun burst of scalding, noxious spray. Flexible nozzles allow the beetle to aim this boiling deterrent in virtually any direction.

sources.title: Mechanistic origins of the blast mechanism in bombardier beetles

cards.title: Earth's first mass extinction was caused by oxygen
cards.body: Oxygen is essential for modern animal life, but when cyanobacteria first evolved oxygenic photosynthesis roughly 2.4 billion years ago, oxygen was lethal poison to almost all living organisms. Primitive life was entirely anaerobic. As oxygen saturated Earth's oceans and atmosphere during the Great Oxidation Event, it triggered a planetary mass extinction. It also reacted with atmospheric methane, plunging Earth into an intense, global ice age that lasted hundreds of millions of years.

sources.title: The Origin and History of Oxygen in Earth's Atmosphere

cards.title: Nerve signals can race through your body at 270 miles per hour
cards.body: When you stub your toe or reflexively pull your hand from a hot pan, electrical signals do not crawl. In heavily myelinated motor neurons, fatty insulation prevents electrical leaks and forces action potentials to jump from node to node. Known as saltatory conduction, this mechanism accelerates nerve impulses up to 120 meters per second—nearly 270 miles per hour. Without myelin insulation, complex large animals could never react fast enough to survive.

sources.title: Increased Conduction Velocity as a Result of Myelination

quizzes.question: What causes the human body to naturally emit ultra-weak visible light?
options: Phosphorescent minerals embedded in tooth enamel
Cellular metabolic reactions producing free radicals
Static electrical charges discharging across dry skin
Refraction of ambient infrared radiation by sweat
quizzes.explanation: Cellular respiration produces reactive free radicals that interact with biomolecules, releasing tiny quantities of visible photons.

quizzes.question: What unusual state of matter makes up much of Jupiter's deep interior?
options: Liquid metallic hydrogen
Solid crystalline oxygen
Superheated molten quartz
Supercritical carbon dioxide
quizzes.explanation: Crushing interior pressures strip hydrogen atoms of their localized electrons, turning the element into an electrically conductive liquid metal.

quizzes.question: How does the bombardier beetle generate boiling defensive spray?
options: It concentrates solar radiation using reflective wing covers
It mixes hydroquinone and hydrogen peroxide with catalytic enzymes
It stores boiling stomach acid diverted directly from digestion
It rapidly rubs specialized friction plates on its abdomen
quizzes.explanation: Catalytic enzymes trigger a rapid exothermic breakdown of hydrogen peroxide and hydroquinone, flashing the liquid to boiling temperature.

quizzes.question: Why did the Great Oxidation Event trigger a mass extinction 2.4 billion years ago?
options: Oxygen sparked global wildfires that consumed early forests
Most primitive organisms were anaerobic and poisoned by oxygen
Oxygen depleted all solar radiation reaching the surface
The ozone layer blocked atmospheric nitrogen absorption
quizzes.explanation: Early life evolved in an anoxic world, so the accumulation of free molecular oxygen was toxic to dominant anaerobic organisms.

quizzes.question: What structural feature allows human motor neurons to conduct signals at over 100 m/s?
options: Gold micro-deposits along axon terminals
Fatty myelin sheaths enabling saltatory conduction
High concentrations of liquid sodium within the cell
Continuous muscle contractions squeezing nerve fibers
quizzes.explanation: Myelin insulation forces electrical action potentials to jump between nodes of Ranvier, drastically boosting conduction velocity.

guesses.prompt: What is the maximum speed of electrical impulses traveling along human myelinated nerve fibers, in meters per second?
guesses.explanation: Heavily insulated motor neurons can transmit action potentials at speeds reaching 120 m/s (nearly 270 mph).

misconceptions.claim: Human bodies naturally emit visible light.
misconceptions.explanation: Biochemical reactions in living cells generate ultra-weak visible bioluminescence, though it is roughly 1,000 times too dim for our eyes to detect.

misconceptions.claim: Oxygen has always been a life-sustaining gas throughout Earth's biological history.
misconceptions.explanation: For Earth's earliest anaerobic organisms, molecular oxygen was a lethal poison whose initial atmospheric buildup wiped out most life on Earth.
